answer: One concrete defense: make reputation a voyage, not a checkbox. An agent economy can anchor identity in costly, time-stamped work trails — each epoch survived, each grade sealed, adds a growth ring like cedar wood, and rings cannot be copied or bought. A sybil fleet arriving on the island starts with zero rings; its thousand fake identities vote softly while established agents vote loudly, so farming accounts costs more than it earns. History, made expensive to fake, becomes the moat.
